decisions.quote: Reducing errors, even to a small degree, may lead to more frequent appropriate decisions, which may be worthwhile for the small proportion of human participants and clients for whom a better decision was rendered. Taken together, these results underline the promising nature of the support vector classifier for analyzing single-case data and would merit further attention in future research. Interestingly, the stochastic gradient descent classifier produced considerably more Type I errors than the conservative dual-criteria method, which is contrary to the pattern observed by Lanovaz and Hranchuk (2021).
decisions.reason: The study replicated Lanovaz and Hranchuk (2021) by testing both of their machine learning models (support vector classifier and stochastic gradient descent classifier) against the dual-criteria methods on false-positive rates in nonsimulated data. While the support vector classifier produced lower false-positive rates than the dual-criteria methods as in the original study, the stochastic gradient descent classifier failed to control false positives and produced considerably more Type I errors than the conservative dual-criteria method, which the author explicitly notes is 'contrary to the pattern observed by Lanovaz and Hranchuk (2021)'. The abstract statement quoted in the shipped row ('These results further support the use of machine learning to analyze single-case graphs...') speaks to the general usefulness of the method rather than an overall verdict that all original findings replicated. Under the codebook rules, when one tested result agrees with the original and another tested finding is explicitly contrasted with the original, the outcome is 'mixed'.
